Examples of patterns of employed masks used on EM grids. A. An 8 × 8 grid of 20 μm circular masks used in the micropatterning procedure. B. An 8 × 8 grid of 30 μm circular masks used in the micropatterning procedure. Set the dose to 900 mJ/mm 2 and enable stitching mode. Switch the fluorescence microscope to the correct optical path, compatible with the PRIMO device. Lock the pattern in place and press start to begin the micropatterning procedure. You should see small spots of light reflecting off the grid surface. This process should take 3–10 min, depending on the size of the pattern and the number of squares that you want to pattern. Immediately remove the grid after the micropatterning procedure is done to avoid excess PLL-g-PEG layer degradation and wash the grid several times in fresh PBS. Place the grids in a fresh 30 mm glass-bottom dish filled with PBS. Wash the glass-bottom dish with the stencil used for micropatterning before repeating the protocol for the other grids. Pause point: The micropatterned grids can be stored in PBS at 4 °C for up to four weeks. Critical: Be careful and avoid grids drying out. Side protocol—micropatterning of grids using PRIMO and PLPP gel: Alternatively, the micropatterning of grids with PRIMO can be done using PLPP gel instead of PLPP ( Engel et al., 2021 ). Indeed, the PLPP photoinitiator from Alvéole is also available in a gel form, which speeds up the photopatterning 30 times in comparison to the liquid form. Another advantage is that you can flip the sample upside down to be able to print on the EM grid bars if needed. The protocol using PLPP gel requires several drying steps of the grid, and the passivation is made with polylysine (PLL) and then mPEG-SVA: As in the regular PLPP procedure described above, glow discharge and place a PDMS stencil on your grid. Grid passivation: incubate your grid with a PLL solution (100 μg/mL for 30 min), rinse three times with 20 mM HEPES at pH = 8.5, and incubate your grid again with a solution of mPEG-SVA (10–20 μL for 1 h). Alternatively, an incubation with PLL-g-PEG can be done as described above. Micropatterning with PRIMO: a drop of PLPP gel (1 μL) is diluted in deionized water (2 μL) and spread on the grid. After the complete drying of the solution, the grid is placed upside down on the microscope deck holder. The steps using the Leonardo software are then similar to the PLPP protocol described above, with significantly lower UV doses (20–40 mJ/mm 2 ). Incubation of grids with fibronectin. Prepare a Petri dish with a small square of parafilm. Place 30 μL drops of fibronectin (50 μg/mL) on the parafilm and place a grid on each drop. Incubate at room temperature for 20–30 min. The fibronectin solution was prepared by diluting the fibronectin stock solution in PBS. Wash the grids twice in PBS for 5 min and once with DMEM before use. Critical: Be careful and avoid grids drying out. Pause point: The grids can be stored for up to seven days in PBS at 4 °C. Critical: Be careful and avoid grids drying out. Seeding mammalian cells on micropatterned grids The next steps are all performed under sterile conditions in a laminar flow hood. Preparing the cells for seeding. Check the cells under a standard microscope for viability and cell health. Our cells were maintained in T75 flasks in 12 mL of DMEM media supplemented with Pen/strep and FCS. Aspirate the media and briefly wash the cells with warm PBS. Add 2 mL of 0.05% trypsin and incubate for several minutes at 37 °C with 5% CO 2 until the cells detach from the dish. Add 5 mL of DMEM, resuspend the cells, and pipette them in a 15 mL Falcon tube. Centrifuge the cells at 500× g for 5 min at 37 °C. Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells carefully in a small amount of fresh, warm DMEM. Pass the entire cell suspension through a 40 μm cell strainer into a new 15 mL Falcon tube to obtain single cells. Mix 10 μL of cell suspension with 10 μL of Trypan Blue and pipette 10 μL of the mixture on a counting slide. Use the cell counter to determine the concentration of living cells in number of cells/mL. Place the micropatterned grids in ~1 mL of DMEM supplemented with Pen/strep and FCS in a fresh 30 mm glass-bottom dish and carefully pipette 200,000 cells dropwise on top of the grids. Ensure the grids are on the bottom of the dish, Quantifoil film up, evenly spaced and a short distance away from the edges of the dish. Incubate the dish with the grids and the cells in the cell incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO 2 . Save the remainder of the cells in a warm place ( Figure 1E ). Critical: Optimize the cell density and incubation time for your cell line. Adding too many cells will lead to cells growing also on areas of the grid covered with an anti-fouling layer. Adding too few cells will lead to reduced throughput and loss of enough sites suitable for FIB milling. Assessment of the grids. After 30–60 min, remove the grids from the incubator and look at them under a light microscope. The cells should be attaching themselves to the areas of the grid that were micropatterned and to the areas of the dish surrounding the grids. When the micropatterned areas do not have a lot of cells, add additional cells dropwise and incubate again. Incubate the cells on the grid 4–5 h before plunge freezing at 37 °C with 5% CO 2 . Vitrification of mammalian cells Turn the vitrobot on and warm the chamber to 37 °C with 85% humidity. Pre-warm some Fluorobrite medium on a small heating plate of the incubator and, when needed, make a suspension of 1 μm FluoSphere fiducials in Fluorobrite medium (1:30). Assemble and cool down the nitrogen container with liquid nitrogen. Once it is cold, fill the ethane container with ethane or ethane/propane mix. The ethane will turn cloudy and freeze on the sides of the cup when the cryogen is at the correct temperature. Place the grids, Fluorobrite medium for washing, and the fiducial suspension on a 37 °C hot plate or small incubator. Place the blotting paper on one blotting pad and a ring of parafilm on the other blotting pad for backside blotting. For each grid, carefully pick the grid up with the vitrobot tweezers by the outer ring, trying not to disturb the Quantifoil film. Attach the tweezers to the vitrobot with the top of the grid and the cells facing towards the pad with the parafilm. Briefly dip the grids in Fluorobrite to remove the autofluorescent DMEM medium. Add 3.6 μL of 1:30 FluorSpheres fiducial suspension right before plunge-freezing. Ensure the suspension is properly mixed by vortexing. Blot the grids for 8.5 s with 10 blot force and 1 drain time. As vitrobot machines are not entirely reproducible, the settings may need to be adjusted when needed to increase or reduce ice thickness. Yearly instrument alignment performed by Thermo Fisher is advisable to help with reproducibility. The blot force can be measured according to the protocol in Sader et al. (2020). Pause point: After plunge-freezing, store the grids in a grid box for unclipped grids in a liquid nitrogen dewar. Thinning of the cells to ~150 nm using cryo FIB–SEM Assessment of ice contamination rate in the FIB–SEM chamber. Notes: Chamber vacuum can affect the contamination rate. Installation of the Delmic CERES ice shield can reduce the contamination rate significantly. Assessment of the contamination rate under different conditions can help determine how long a user can mill the grid without the lamellae deteriorating to an unusable thickness ( Figure 3 ). Figure

Bottom: a typical EM grid that was incubated with human mesenchymal stem cells. B. Bottom: photopatterned EM grid with centrally adhered RPE-1 cells. C. Top: two touching 20 μm diameter circles were patterned in the center of all grid squares to align cell adherence to allow for milling from different angles. Bottom: an EM grid that was photopatterned with the PRIMO system. Possible milling sites are indicated with red arrows. Load an empty, clipped grid into the FIB–SEM. Navigate to an area in the center of the grid, focus, and determine eucentric height. Use a stage rotation of 110° and a stage tilt of 30°. For the full procedure, see details below. Set the magnification to cover approximately 4 μm horizontal field width (HFW) and image with the electron beam. Focus on the film next to the holes. Use a scan rotation of 0°. Pick two holes in the support film close to the top of the grid and measure the thickness of the film on the edge of the holes. Repeat this for two holes in the center of the grid and two holes close to the bottom of the grid. Wait a fixed amount of time and repeat the procedure. Imaging the same area multiple times could shrink the built-up ice layer. To avoid this, after each timepoint, use a different set of holes to do the measurement. Plot the data in a graph and calculate the slope to obtain the contamination rate. Selection and preparation of sites appropriate for milling. Preparing the cryo FIB–SEM: i. Wake up the system in the xT microscope Control software. ii. In the Beam Control tab, select Sputter Vacuum and purge the lines five times. This should take approximately 20 min. Return to High Vacuum when done. iii. In the Cryo TEM Preparation tab, purge the GIS lines for 30 s. iv. Fill the dewar with liquid nitrogen and place the heat exchanger inside to cool down the system. Clipping the grids: i. Follow Thermo Fisher’s procedure to clip the grids. Critical: Work carefully to avoid buildup of ice contamination on the grids. ii. Use special Auto-grid rings with a cutout to improve grid access. Mark the edges of the ring with a black or blue marker to help position the grids in the autoloader of the TEM microscope. iii. Save the grids in a grid box for AutoGrids under liquid nitrogen. Loading the grids into the FIB–SEM: i. Cool down the loading station and insert a pre-tilted shuttle. ii. Once it is cooled down, place the grid boxes into the station and load two grids into the shuttle. Ensure that the Autogrid cutout is positioned perfectly at the top. Work carefully to avoid buildup of ice contamination on the grids. iii. Quickly load the shuttle into the FIB–SEM chamber and check proper position using the in-chamber camera before disconnecting the transfer rod. Atlas acquisition: i. Move the shuttle to the mapping position in the chamber using the xT Microscope Control software. It may help to set the scan rotation for the ion and electron beams to 180° for easier visualization. ii. Using the SEM beam and the Everhart-Thornley detector (ETD), focus the beam on the grid and correct for astigmatism. Use a 2 kV beam at 25 pA for samples with thin ice and a 5 kV beam for samples with thicker ice. iii. Open MAPS software and take a snapshot of the whole grid. iv. Place a tile set on the center of the grid, 5 × 7 tiles with a tile height of 600 μm HFW and a total HFW of 2.76 mm. Set the resolution to 3,072 × 2,048, the pixel size to 195 nm, and the dwell time to 1 us. Start the acquisition. Eucentric height and milling angle determination: i. Mark the potential milling sites in the MAPS software by clicking Add Lamella Site Here . Ideally, these are single cells that are positioned in the middle of the grid squares, without any ice contamination on top. Only squares close to the center of the grid should ideally be selected, as the sites close to the Autogrid ring will yield small lamellae due to a high milling angle. ii. Navigate to each site using the Drive To Mapping Position button, increase the magnification of the SEM beam, and focus the beam on the carbon film. Use 2–5 kV, 13 pA, and a 300 ns dwell time. While in live mode, link z . iii. Determine the eucentric height of each milling site using a manual approach; the prompts are available in MAPS or the automated procedure is available in AutoTEM. Turn on the ion beam and use the ETD detector to image each site. Focus the beam. Use 30 kV, 30 pA, and 100 ns dwell time. Tilt the stage to 20° and image the site. If the edge of the Autogrid ring is in view, increase the tilt angle. When it is not in view, decrease the angle. From the point where the edge of the Autogrid ring is in view, tilt up 1–2° to get sufficient clearance for the ion beam not to be deflected. Mark this milling angle in MAPS software by clicking Store Angle . The icon next to the name of the lamella site will change from orange to green. iv. Mark each site at the eucentric height and the milling angle in the FIB–SEM GUI for easier navigation later. Assessment of milling sites by the METEOR system. Make sure the z-height of the stage is linked in the microscope GUI. Open the ODEMIS software on the METEOR microscope PC and make a new project folder. Press FM imaging to move the stage to the METEOR position and insert the objective lens (LMPLFLN 50×/NA = 0.5/WD = 10.6 mm). Add imaging streams for each fluorophore, select the power for each channel, and set the exposure time to ~300 μs. Usually, 200–400 mW is sufficient, depending on the fluorophore, the abundance of the ROI, and the camera on the system. Focus the image using the autofluorescence signal in the green channel by slowly approaching the sample with the objective lens until the signal inside the target cell is sharp or until you can see the holes in the Quantifoil support film due to its autofluorescent properties. Critical: Do not insert the objective lens too far, as it can crash into the shuttle and damage the lens. Acquire an image of each lamella site to confirm the presence of your ROI in the cells. A good start for camera settings is: bin 1, resolution 1,190 × 928 px, a gain of 16-bit, and a readout rate of 310 MHz. Adjust the exposure time and the power in the rest of the channels to a value that will yield a clear signal but not an oversaturated histogram. Save these imaging positions in the FIB–SEM xT Microscope Control software for easier navigation later. Switch back to the milling site in the chamber by pressing SEM imaging . Wait for the objective lens to retract and the shuttle to move back to the milling position in the chamber. Navigate to the next milling position using MAPS or the saved positions in the xT Microscope Control software and repeat Steps D3d–D3f. Setup of batch milling protocol. Open AutoTEM. It should read in all the positions from the MAPS software. Apply a template with the following parameters ( Table 2 ) to all sites. Table

steps.title: Glow‑discharge EM grids
steps.instruction: Place 200 mesh gold Quantifoil R2/1 grids (SiO₂ support) in a holder or on a parafilm‑covered glass slide and glow‑discharge both sides in a Pelco easiGlow plasma cleaner at 15 mA, 0.4 mBar for 60–90 s with a 10 s hold; repeat on the opposite side using the same settings.

steps.title: Apply PLL‑g‑PEG anti‑fouling layer
steps.instruction: On a sheet of parafilm in a Petri dish, dispense 30 µL drops of 0.5 mg/mL PLL‑g‑PEG in PBS; place each grid into a drop, blot excess PBS (do not dry completely), and incubate the grids overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash and store grids in PBS
steps.instruction: Vertically dip the grids several times in PBS to remove unbound PLL‑g‑PEG, then keep them in a PBS‑filled dish; grids may be stored at 4 °C for several days.

steps.title: Set up PRIMO microscope and calibrate
steps.instruction: Turn on the fluorescence microscope and PC, insert a 20× S Plan Fluor ELWD (0.45 NA) objective, focus on a black cross drawn on a glass‑bottom dish, set the perfect‑focus system at that Z‑height, open Leonardo software, click “Calibrate tube lens”, choose a calibration pattern (preferably with 1 µm features), adjust laser power and exposure until the smallest features are visible, verify pixel ratio and laser power on the DMD wheel.

steps.title: Apply PLPP and perform UV patterning
steps.instruction: Place a PRIMO stencil with 4 mm circular holes in a new 30 mm glass‑bottom dish, pipette 2 µL PLPP into each hole, blot each grid lightly (do not dry), then place the grid in the PLPP droplet, cover the dish, and locate the grid in reflected‑light mode. Load the .png pattern (125 DPI) in Leonardo, position it over the grid squares, set dose to 900 mJ mm⁻², enable stitching, lock the pattern, and start UV micropatterning (3–10 min).

substeps.instruction: After patterning, immediately remove the grid, wash several times in fresh PBS, and place it in a fresh 30 mm glass‑bottom dish filled with PBS.
Grids may be stored at 4 °C in PBS for up to four weeks; avoid drying.

steps.title: Alternative PLPP‑gel patterning (optional)
steps.instruction: Glow‑discharge grids, place a PDMS stencil, incubate with 100 µg/mL PLL for 30 min, rinse three times with 20 mM HEPES pH 8.5, incubate with 10–20 µL mPEG‑SVA for 1 h, then apply 1 µL PLPP‑gel diluted 1 µL + 2 µL deionised water, dry, flip the grid upside‑down, and perform UV patterning with Leonardo using 20–40 mJ mm⁻² dose.

steps.title: Incubate grids with fibronectin
steps.instruction: Prepare a Petri dish with a parafilm square, place 30 µL drops of 50 µg/mL fibronectin (PBS‑diluted stock) on the parafilm, lay a grid into each drop, and incubate at room temperature for 20–30 min.

substeps.instruction: Wash grids twice in PBS for 5 min each, then once in DMEM; avoid drying.
Grids can be stored at 4 °C in PBS for up to seven days.

steps.title: Seed mammalian cells on patterned grids
steps.instruction: In a laminar‑flow hood, detach RPE‑1 cells from a T75 flask grown in DMEM/F‑12 + Pen/Strep + FCS by washing with warm PBS, adding 2 mL 0.05 % trypsin, incubating at 37 °C/5 % CO₂ until detached, neutralising with 5 mL DMEM, centrifuging 500 × g for 5 min at 37 °C, resuspending in warm DMEM, filtering through a 40 µm strainer, counting live cells with Trypan Blue, and adding 200 000 cells in ~1 mL DMEM + Pen/Strep + FCS dropwise onto each grid placed bottom‑up in a fresh 30 mm glass‑bottom dish.

substeps.instruction: Incubate the dish at 37 °C/5 % CO₂; optimise cell density to avoid over‑growth on anti‑fouling areas.

steps.title: Assess cell attachment and incubate further
steps.instruction: After 30–60 min, inspect grids under a light microscope; if patterned areas lack cells, add more cells dropwise and re‑incubate. Continue incubation for 4–5 h at 37 °C/5 % CO₂ before plunge‑freezing.

steps.title: Plunge‑freeze grids with vitrobot
steps.instruction: Warm the Vitrobot chamber to 37 °C, 85 % humidity; pre‑warm Fluorobrite medium and prepare a 1 µm FluoSphere fiducial suspension (1:30 in Fluorobrite). Fill the ethane (or 37 % ethane/63 % propane) cup until the ethane clouds. Place each grid on a parafilm‑lined blotting pad, dip briefly in Fluorobrite to remove DMEM, add 3.6 µL fiducial suspension, blot for 8.5 s with blot force 10 and drain time 1 s, then plunge into ethane. Store vitrified grids in a liquid‑nitrogen‑filled grid box for unclipped grids.

steps.title: Prepare FIB‑SEM system
steps.instruction: Wake the xT microscope control software, select Sputter Vacuum in Beam Control and purge lines five times (~20 min), purge GIS lines 30 s in Cryo TEM Preparation, fill the dewar with liquid N₂ and insert the heat exchanger to cool the system.

steps.title: Clip grids and load into FIB‑SEM
steps.instruction: Clip each grid according to Thermo Fisher’s procedure using Auto‑grid rings with cutouts, mark ring edges with a black/blue marker, place clipped grids in a grid box for AutoGrids, cool the loading station, insert a pre‑tilted shuttle, load two grids ensuring the Autogrid cutout is at the top, then quickly insert the shuttle into the FIB‑SEM chamber and verify position with the in‑chamber camera.

steps.title: Acquire grid atlas mapping
steps.instruction: Move the shuttle to the mapping position, set SEM beam to 2 kV/25 pA (thin ice) or 5 kV (thick ice), focus, correct astigmatism, open MAPS, acquire a whole‑grid snapshot, then tile the centre (5 × 7 tiles, 600 µm HFW each, total 2.76 mm HFW) at 3 072 × 2 048 pixels, 195 nm pixel size, 1 µs dwell.

steps.title: Select milling sites and set eucentric height
steps.instruction: In MAPS, add lamella sites on single cells near the centre of grid squares, navigate to each site, increase SEM magnification, focus on carbon film (2–5 kV, 13 pA, 300 ns dwell), link Z‑height, then determine eucentric height manually (or via AutoTEM). Turn on the ion beam, image with 30 kV/30 pA, 100 ns dwell, tilt stage to ~20°, adjust tilt until the Autogrid ring edge is just in view, then increase tilt 1–2° for clearance and store the angle in MAPS (icon turns green).

steps.title: Assess ice contamination rate (optional)
steps.instruction: Load an empty clipped grid, navigate to centre, set stage rotation 110° and tilt 30°, image holes at top, centre, and bottom of the grid at a fixed interval, measure film thickness over time, plot thickness vs. time to calculate contamination rate (e.g., 3 nm h⁻¹ before CERES, 0.6 nm h⁻¹ after).

steps.title: Configure batch milling parameters in AutoTEM
steps.instruction: Open AutoTEM, import positions from MAPS, apply the template with the following parameters: Preparation Ion HFW Oversize 80 µm, Eucentric Tilt disabled, etc. (see full Table 2 for Rough, Medium, Fine, and Finer milling settings, including pattern offsets, overlaps, depths, currents, DCM rescan intervals, and pattern types).

steps.title: Run rough milling and GIS deposition
steps.instruction: In AutoTEM, enable only the Preparation (Rough Milling) tab, ensure all sites are selected, click Run, then deposit a GIS layer on the grid for 8 s (no‑lift‑out system) or 90 s (lift‑out system). Fill the FIB‑SEM dewar with liquid N₂ before starting the automated rough‑milling program; the CERES ice shield will insert automatically.

steps.title: Image lamella sites with METEOR
steps.instruction: Link stage Z‑height in the microscope GUI, open ODEMIS, create a new project, switch to FM imaging, insert the LMPLFLN 50×/0.5 NA objective, add imaging streams for each fluorophore (200–400 mW, ~300 µs exposure), focus using green autofluorescence or Quantifoil hole fluorescence, acquire images of each lamella site, and save positions in xT control for later navigation.

steps.title: Polish lamellae to final thickness
steps.instruction: In AutoTEM, navigate to each site, focus the ion beam, and perform step‑wise polishing with a 30 kV ion beam: start at 30 pA using two rectangular boxes ~300 nm apart, monitor lamella integrity, then move boxes to ~200 nm apart, repeat; finally lower current to 10 pA, bring boxes to ~150 nm or less, and continue thinning. If the GIS layer degrades, add an over‑tilt of +0.5°–1° and mill from the top at 10 pA only. Estimate lamella thickness by imaging at 5 kV (dark gray at ~250–300 nm) and 2 kV (lighter) and stop when 150–200 nm is reached.

steps.title: Final METEOR imaging of polished lamellae
steps.instruction: Return to METOR, insert the objective lens, use the same imaging streams (≈300 µs exposure), focus via green autofluorescence, acquire images of each lamella to confirm ROI presence (exposures up to 30 s may be needed for weak signals), retract the lens 5–10 mm before moving to the next site, and export all images as print‑ready TIFFs after histogram adjustment.

steps.title: Sputter coat lamellae with platinum
steps.instruction: In the Cryo TEM Preparation tab, click “Prepare For Sputtering”, wait until chamber pressure reaches 0.1 mbar, then sputter at 7 mA for 5–7 s (confirm by white glow on in‑chamber camera), then press “Recover From Sputtering” to return to high vacuum.

steps.title: Unload grids and store for TEM
steps.instruction: Cool the loading station, remove the shuttle from the FIB‑SEM, place it in the loading station, flip the shuttle 90°, carefully transfer the clipped grids into a grid box for clipped grids, avoid ice contamination, and store the box under clean liquid nitrogen until TEM imaging. Finally, warm the FIB‑SEM chamber to room temperature by removing the heat exchanger and putting the system to “sleep”.
